claims.wording: Depflush advertises version 1.3.1 for macOS 14 or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel.
claims.excerpt: Version 1.3.1 · macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel · Open source (GPL-3.0)
claims.conditions: Advertised version, not independently certified latest binary or runtime compatibility

claims.wording: The app is advertised as free with no account; donations are optional.
claims.conditions: No payment or donation flow tested; no paid plan verified

claims.wording: Depflush publishes its source under GPL-3.0; its name and icon are excluded from that licence.
claims.excerpt: The source code is released under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE).
claims.supportingExcerpt: They are not licensed under the GPL.
claims.conditions: Do not extend source-code licence to website screenshots or trademarks

claims.wording: Dormant dependency discovery targets vendor next to composer.lock and node_modules next to package.json; the advertised default inactivity threshold is 12 months and is configurable.
claims.excerpt: vendor folders next to a composer.lock and node_modules next to a package.json, in projects you haven't changed for 12 months. You choose the threshold.
claims.conditions: FAQ says vendor, node_modules, var and .git are ignored for inactivity. Reinstallation depends on registries, credentials and compatible tooling; no guaranteed recovery

claims.wording: The documented Docker view preselects rebuildable cache/registry images, but leaves locally built images, stopped containers and orphaned volumes unticked with warnings.
claims.excerpt: Images you built yourself, stopped containers and orphaned volumes are listed with a warning and stay unticked.
claims.conditions: Docker must run for inspection; do not delete Docker.raw or imply a guaranteed reduction

claims.wording: Depflush documents item/path/size preview and confirmation, Trash by default, and optional permanent deletion in Settings.
claims.excerpt: Every item is listed with its path and size. You confirm the total before anything happens.
claims.supportingExcerpt: Files go to the Trash, so you can put them back. Switch to permanent deletion in Settings when you want the space right away.
claims.conditions: Not a safety guarantee; Trash bytes are not newly available disk space. No deletion performed

claims.wording: The vendor says scan and cleanup run locally, without an account, analytics or network calls; it also documents communication with the local Docker installation.
claims.excerpt: There is no account, no analytics and no crash reporting. The app only reads file sizes on your Mac and talks to your local Docker installation.
claims.conditions: Downloads, package restoration and registry pulls can require internet; do not claim all associated developer workflows are offline

claims.wording: Depflush documents a menu-bar free-space display and configurable low-space notifications, defaulting to 20 GB.
claims.excerpt: When it drops below the limit you set, 20 GB by default, you get a notification and can open the scan with one click.
claims.conditions: Not proof of per-app historical growth attribution or tested notification delivery

claims.wording: The official installation documentation says Depflush is not yet Apple-notarized; Full Disk Access is optional for Mail and iPhone backup size visibility.
claims.excerpt: Depflush is not yet notarized by Apple
claims.supportingExcerpt: Optional: grant Full Disk Access in Settings to see the size of Mail and iPhone backups as well.
claims.conditions: No binary signature inspected. Disclose warning; do not repeat protection-bypass instructions. Binary runtime requirements beyond macOS not verified

claims.wording: The vendor documents SHA-256 duplicate SQL-dump checking for dumps over 100 MB; exact duplicate photos/videos are separate from similar-photo detection.
claims.excerpt: Dumps over 100 MB are compared by size, then by SHA-256.
claims.supportingExcerpt: It compares photos and videos in Pictures, Movies, Documents, Desktop and Downloads byte for byte, so only true copies are listed, never similar-looking pictures.
claims.conditions: Do not certify deletion safety or duplicate accuracy without testing

claims.wording: Depflush's official screenshots are labelled sample data.
claims.excerpt: Safe items are ticked, anything you might still need is not, and each list says how to get it back. Sample data shown.
claims.conditions: Image capture date/version unknown; not our scan results

claims.wording: The official homepage links to cypriennkeneng/depflush; that repository links back to depflush.com and names Web Loupe (Cyprien Nkeneng).
claims.conditions: Official snapshot links corroborate repository identity; no current alias established

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a macOS 13+ preview; the identified release is 0.1.0-preview.1, advertised universal, Apple Development signed but not Developer ID signed or notarized, with physical Intel/clean-machine validation incomplete.
claims.excerpt: Published preview says **Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**.
claims.conditions: Register sections Preview, installation and runtime caveats and Unverified claims; not a new binary test

claims.wording: Breathing Room advertises a free local core and optional AI Care at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year; hosted AI requires internet and authentication.
claims.conditions: Renewal until cancellation; applicable checkout tax. Quotas/entitlement enforcement unverified; hosted requests may include paths, process/storage data

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements storage views, grouped helper CPU/memory, sampled activity and exact-action review; this is not distributed-binary parity evidence.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer.
claims.conditions: Register Current capability matrix; do not promise attribution, speed or savings. Ruff automatic opt-in and daily exact approvals have different boundaries

claims.wording: Breathing Room discloses Python 3.10+ for inventory/legacy scripts, running-app requirements for daily care, website account-gated downloads and ungated public GitHub release downloads.
claims.excerpt: Python **3.10+** is a disclosed prerequisite for disk inventory and legacy scripts, not bundled.
claims.conditions: Register Preview, installation and runtime caveats and Pricing/access. No account creation or end-to-end hosted testing performed

workflow.title: Dormant project or irreplaceable build? Review developer storage before cleanup
workflow.primaryIntent: Mac developer triage of old dependencies, Docker objects and SQL dumps before granting cleanup approval
workflow.leadDirection: Treat untouched dependencies as rebuild candidates, not permission to remove every large developer folder. Confirm a working restoration path before approving anything.
outline: Show official sample-data Development view after lead only once rights are cleared
Check project metadata, inactivity threshold and registry/tool availability
Separate reproducible dependencies from local changes and unique SQL backups
Distinguish registry Docker images/build cache from local images, containers and volumes
Review path, size, selection and Trash/permanent-delete mode
Choose a focused local cleaner or broader preview investigation with caveats; disclose affiliation
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a non-mutating checklist: unique data? backed up? restorable version/source? rebuild/download cost? exact selection reviewed? No deletion commands or pretend scanner.
